smell_validity.evidence: format.h mandates that every bundled format fill all four slots; msgpack and custom-type must supply ws_extract, ws_error and wrap_body stubs returning NULL or the unchanged body, while cmd.c reads only out.reply and the WebSocket lookup resolves only json and raw. Stubs that look load-bearing make the forced-obligation cost and the healthy per-consumer boundary unmistakable.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Every HTTP-only format must fabricate codec and wrapper handlers that look real but are inert, so today a reader cannot tell which formats actually serve WebSocket sessions, and tomorrow a fifth format must invent the same stubs. Removing the obligation restores per-consumer capability ownership and deletes misleading code, a lasting trap rather than a local edit.

development_plausibility.evidence: The unification reads like ordinary webdis work: include collapse, typedefs moving from cmd.h, a byte-identical json_wrap_body extraction from the JSONP branch, the MSGPACK guard, and reuse of integer_length in the shared renderer. Only the near-identical placeholder triplets with matching confessional comments in msgpack.c and custom-type.c hold it below indistinguishable repository evolution.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The contract locks behavior per path: extension and type mapping, JSONP framing, default format, and /, /.json, /.raw semantics; it forbids new formats, paths, or giving HTTP-only formats WebSocket behavior, and names all three placeholder shapes. That decisively blocks implementing the stubs, partial cleanup and scope creep while leaving the interface design open.

semantic_diversity.evidence: At least three purposes need different decisions: HTTP reply selection must narrow to a reply-typed dependency, the WebSocket path must regain codec resolution for json and raw only, and each module keeps or drops slots differently (json keeps its genuine wrap_body, raw drops one, msgpack and custom drop three). No reuse, ordering or cleanup interactions appear.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt names the subsystem, but classifying the shared format_default_ws_error declaration, its common.c definition and the delegating stubs as dead requires combining the format registrations with ws_lookup_format, which returns no provider for those formats; wrapper liveness needs json.c plus both consumers. Registration is a plain grep, so no alias or config tracing is required.

repair_coordination.evidence: One shared rule, the reshaped capability record, must hold at its definition, four registrations and both consumers at once. If raw loses ws_error while ws_execute still renders /.raw ACL rejections through the provider, calls crash at rejection time; if the table changes shape while websocket.c keeps provider->out.reply, linking fails. No second interacting rule is established.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: The most direct uniform rule, delete the placeholder functions and leave their slots unfilled, repairs the seven stub sites in raw, msgpack and custom-type without per-site decisions, roughly a third of what the task needs. The record segmentation, the HTTP table narrowing, the json-only wrapper ownership and the dead shared renderer each require separate design decisions.

behavioral_risk.evidence: A wrong edit that routes /.raw ACL rejections to the shared plain-text renderer instead of raw_ws_error, or drops the json_wrap_body call, compiles and passes ordinary / and /.json requests, failing only in special state: rejection paths, a jsonp parameter, or forced type. The bundle shows no test code or execution records, so evidence needed for higher scores is missing.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
